ceremony.scoped_git_commit._rationale: C5 (docs/plans/2026-08-21-the-commit-path-reads-git-state-without-spawning-git.md), re-baselined DOWNWARD 2026-08-21 by DIRECT MEASUREMENT against `test_commit_e2e_spawn_budget.py`'s own five fixtures (deterministic across two independent full-suite runs, zero lock-retries observed on any shape), superseding the entry immediately below without ever having shipped green: that entry's 'seam keys unchanged, only op_total moves by 1' premise was written from C2-C4's PLANNED shape, not measured against the LANDED code (f89a4fb31, 69f92af34), and this re-baseline is the actual measurement, run against the manifest before this edit landed (every measured figure failed the shipped assertion at seam AND at op_total). CORRECTED BY THE EM 2026-08-21, SAME DAY, BEFORE THIS ENTRY EVER SHIPPED AS TRUTH: this -5 is NOT a -5 of real processes and must not be read as one. It is the measured fall in seam-VISIBLE calls, and most of it is RE-ROUTING, not removal. C2-C4's re-pointed reads reach the process boundary through `coordinator_core/git/git_state.py::head_blobs` -> `coordinator_core/git/run.py::run_git`, which calls `subprocess.run` directly and never goes through the `git_native._git` name the seam counter wraps. So those spawns LEFT THE COUNTED SEAM AND KEPT SPAWNING. The op_total keys are the honest instrument here (they substitute the `subprocess.run` module attribute AND `Popen`), and they are what a reader should quote -- `commit_gates` binds `_git` by direct import at module load (per this chunk's own dispatch brief), so ITS spawns were never on the seam either way, but the other four sites plainly were, and removing their per-invocation reads removed that many seam calls. The OP_TOTAL keys move by a SMALLER, DIFFERENT amount on three shapes and by a THIRD, still-different amount on the fourth -- op_total_green_path/op_total_directory_pathspec_expansion fall by only 1 (21->20, 22->21) each, op_total_push_raced_path/op_total_pending_drain_superseded fall by 3 (26->23, 37->34), and op_total_deferred_diverged_detach does not move at all (25->25). ATTRIBUTION OF WHY THE OP_TOTAL DELTA IS SMALLER THAN THE SEAM DELTA IS NOW RESOLVED -- it was recorded as an OPEN QUESTION by C5 and answered by the EM the same day, by running the gate that exists for exactly this. `coordinator_core/tests/test_no_uncounted_spawn_on_budgeted_path.py` went RED on this change and named the site by line: `[ceremony.scoped_git_commit] coordinator_core/git/run.py:370 enclosing='run_git' argv0='git'` -- a spawn site reachable from this op's budgeted entrypoint and invisible to its seam counter. That IS the mechanism. C5's candidate (b) ('a second, offsetting spawn was added to the op_total-visible bypass surface in the same window C2-C4 removed seam spawns') was correct in shape; the offsetting spawns are the retained `ls-tree` HEAD reads themselves, now routed through `run_git` instead of `_git`. Candidate (a) (a `diverging_paths` regression) is WITHDRAWN and should not be chased. THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS, stated so no later reader has to re-derive it: on the green path this workstream removed ONE process end-to-end (op_total 21->20), not five. The plan's AC1 -- '17 reads -> 2-3 read spawns' -- is NOT MET by C1-C5 as decomposed, and nothing in this manifest should be read as evidence that it was. The structural reason is worth carrying forward: `head_blobs` retains one spawn PER CALL, so re-pointing another guard onto it ADDS a process while removing an index read. Index-vs-HEAD questions are genuinely free (`read_index` is an in-process parse, measured 24.1ms over this repo's 31,520-entry index and byte-exact against `git ls-files -s`); every HEAD-TREE question still costs a process. A future chunk that re-points more guards at `head_blobs` will move the seam figure down and the op_total figure UP. The `refusal_path_unanswerable=0` key is untouched -- that path short-circuits `_handler` before any spawn, seam or bypass, and this measurement pass did not exercise it (unchanged from every prior baseline). Deliberately NOT chased further under this chunk's own anti-scope: `dirty_tree_gate`'s worktree axis and EOL-phantom filter, `deletion_block_gate`'s `--find-renames` name-status call, and `_reject_stale_index_paths`' worktree-vs-HEAD probe -- named in this chunk's dispatch brief as the three spawns KEPT deliberately by C2-C4, not defects. Prior entry follows, retained as provenance though its 'seam unchanged' claim is now known wrong.  Re-baselined UPWARD 2026-08-21 (opro-03 follow-up, stack-recording-`subprocess.run`-wrapper origin diff against this fixture, four independent measurements per shape): green_path 16->19, directory_pathspec_expansion 17->20, push_raced_path 19->22, pending_drain_superseded 22->25, and every op_total_ key by +1 (NOT +3 -- WHY the op_total delta is smaller than the seam delta is NOT established by the evidence in hand. The two new seam calls are net-new spawns added by the two 2026-08-20 commits named below, so they cannot have been 'previously counted' as anything, op_total included -- and by construction op_total is a superset of the seam (see `_op_total_rationale` below), so three confirmed new seam-routed spawns should raise op_total by at least 3, not 1, on a pure count basis. The nondeterminism note below establishes only that THIS DAY'S op_total measurement fluctuated between budgeted+3 (once, uninstrumented) and budgeted+1 (a dozen times, after `run_with_lock_retry` retries are attributed and subtracted) -- that resolves a within-day measurement artifact, not the gap between this baseline and the prior 2026-08-19, pre-retry-subtraction one. Whether that gap is a genuine spawn-accounting difference or an artifact of comparing an uncorrected old baseline against a corrected new one has not been re-measured under matched methodology, and is an OPEN QUESTION, not a resolved one). Two commits landed on THIS branch between the 2026-08-19 baseline below and today, each adding an UNCONDITIONAL `git_native._git`-routed spawn to every `commit_scoped()`/`_handler()` invocation, regardless of shape: (1) `323aafaf8` ('ceremony: commit_scoped observes mode, so a mode delta can actually land', 2026-08-20 09:40) added `_mode_delta_paths_chunked()`, one `git diff --cached --raw` call (DR-151 mode-preservation fix, `commit_scoped`'s own docstring: 'same chunked seam, no new per-path spawn' -- true per-path, but +1 per invocation regardless of path count). (2) `82dc080eb` ('fix(break-class): ... refuse a stale-index commit', 2026-08-20 18:32) added `scoped_git_commit._reject_stale_index_paths()`, two batched calls (`git diff --name-only HEAD` and `git diff --cached --name-only HEAD`, both regardless of path count) guarding the `state/bug-backlog/2026-08-19-shared-git-index-holds-stale-pre-head-sn-b5b83e42e275.yaml` stale-index-revert bug (falsified before landing per that commit's own message). Neither commit updated this file's spawn_count_budget in the same commit -- this module carries `pytest.mark.cadence`, so the fast tier never ran the assertion that would have caught it, the exact failure class this file's own text already warned about (see 're-baselined 2026-08-18' paragraph below). Both additions are legitimate, deliberate, evidenced break-class fixes, not bugs -- the fix here is to correct the stale figure, not to revert either commit. RESOLVED NONDETERMINISM (found during this re-baseline, mechanism CONFIRMED, disposition implemented in test code -- not a manifest-number question at all in the end). The OP_TOTAL (not seam) figure was observed at budgeted+3 exactly once, in the first measurement pass of the day (before any of this re-baseline's instrumentation existed), uniformly across all four shapes simultaneously; roughly a dozen measurements since (single pytest re-runs plus an 8x same-fixture loop run inside ONE interpreter, fresh tmp repo per iteration) landed on budgeted+1 every time, with zero variance -- see FALSIFICATION METHOD below. The seam figure was rock-stable at the values above across EVERY run, including the +3 one. TWO HYPOTHESES CHECKED, ONE CONFIRMED. (1) `coordinator_core/git/ls_files.py::_tracked_files_cached`, a process-lifetime `lru_cache`-wrapped `subprocess.run` spawn keyed on `(repo_root, pathspec)` -- REFUTED: grepped every import of `coordinator_core.git.ls_files`/`ls_files_bytes` repo-wide; only `ops/eol/census.py` and a test file import it, neither reachable from `ceremony.scoped_git_commit`'s `_handler`. A real, legitimate module, simply not on this op's path. (2) `coordinator_core/git_lock_retry.py::run_with_lock_retry`, wired into `git_native.py::_git()`'s `_invoke` closure (`result = _invoke() if not capture else run_with_lock_retry(_invoke)`, the exact call-site every origin trace pointed at) -- CONFIRMED as the mechanism: it retries the SAME `_invoke()` (a real second, third, ... `subprocess.run`) up to `DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS=8` times on genuine `.git/index.lock` contention (this repo is a deliberately shared working tree by design, per that module's own docstring -- a real, production-observed hazard even against an isolated `tmp_path` repo, e.g. Windows Defender's real-time scan on a freshly-written `.git` object/lock file). Because the retry happens INSIDE `_invoke`, the SEAM counter (which wraps only the outer `_git()` call once) cannot see it while the global `subprocess.run` counter can -- this is EXACTLY why the seam figure stayed rock-stable while op_total moved, resolving what an earlier pass here mis-scoped as a bypass-side-only phenomenon and wrongly suspected `session/scope.py::_git_run`/claim-release cost on. That claim-release suspicion is WITHDRAWN, explicitly, so nobody chases it: the confirmed mechanism is `run_with_lock_retry`, not ambient claim-count state. FALSIFICATION METHOD (recorded so it is not re-walked): a standalone script ran the green_path shape 8x back-to-back in ONE interpreter process, a fresh `tmp_path`-equivalent repo per iteration, under a stack-recording `subprocess.run` wrapper; origin multisets were diffed pairwise across all 8 iterations (iteration 0 vs each of 1-7, and each consecutive pair). Result: byte-identical call SHAPE and COUNT every time (total=22 all 8x; only expected per-run noise -- tmp paths, commit shas -- differed). This ruled out any first-call/warm-up/order-dependent mechanism keyed on something constant across iterations (a real-repo-root-keyed cache would show iteration 0 differing from 1-7; it did not) -- which is what sent the search to `git_lock_retry` instead. DISPOSITION (ratified, implemented): NOT a documented tolerance and NOT an accepted-outlier shrug -- this gate's own operational definition of 'counted' forbids a bound, a range, or a `<=` (module docstring, 'THIS GATE'S OPERATIONAL DEFINITION OF COUNTED'): a new spawn must FAIL something, not fit under something. Instead, `test_commit_e2e_spawn_budget.py::_count_op_spawns_both_ways` now wraps `git_native.run_with_lock_retry` (the NAME `_git()` calls, patched only in `git_native`'s own namespace -- `git_lock_retry.py` itself is never touched, since it is a real resilience mechanism for a real hazard and the test adapts to it, not the reverse) and MEASURES each attempt beyond the first per `_git()` call as an attributed `retries_fired` count, asserted bounded by `DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS`. `_assert_op_total` then asserts EXACT equality of `n_all - retries_fired` against the budgeted figure below -- still exact equality, against the op's actual spawn count with a measured, attributed, non-op-path event subtracted, never a fudge factor. A genuinely new spawn is never mistaken for a retry (it was never observed inside `run_with_lock_retry`) and still fails the assertion. Nonzero `retries_fired` prints loudly rather than being silently absorbed. STANDING NOTE for whoever next reads this file: `op_total_*` counts retries by construction, so EVERY `op_total_*` key in this manifest (not only these four) is contention-inflated on a shared tree whenever `run_with_lock_retry` fires -- named here once so it is not rediscovered from scratch on a different op. This is a REDUCTION, not a bound fitted to an unreduced set -- the skipped reads are skipped only when their sole consumer would iterate an empty claim list, and a Kept-bearing message still pays both. ceremony.scoped_git_commit._op_total_rationale: opro-03 C6, measured 2026-08-19 on this repo. TWO LAYERS OF KEY, deliberately, and they must not be collapsed. The bare shape keys (green_path/directory_pathspec_expansion/push_raced_path/pending_drain_superseded) count the `git_native._git` NATIVE-GIT seam, via a function-OBJECT substitution in test_commit_e2e_spawn_budget.py -- mechanism-robust but ROUTING-NARROW: a spawn that reaches the process boundary without going through `_git()` is invisible to them by construction. The op does exactly that in three measured places reachable from `_handler` (`session/scope.py::_git_run` via claim release, `hooks/auto_push.py::_run_git` via `run_commit_pipeline` -> `_drain_pending_push_after_sync`, and `git/divergence.py::_run_git`), so those legs could grow without bound and the seam figures would never move. The op_total_* keys close that: counted by substituting the `subprocess.run` MODULE ATTRIBUTE, scoped to the op invocation only (a test-scoped counter would be mostly fixture -- 28/29/37 per test versus these op-only figures). Deltas over the seam figures are +6/+6/+8 and that GAP IS THE POINT: it is the uncounted-bypass surface enumerated by coordinator_core/tests/test_no_uncounted_spawn_on_budgeted_path.py. Shrinking it by routing a bypass through the counted seam is progress; shrinking it by editing these numbers is the failure this plan's anti-scope names. No spawn was added by any of this -- each key makes existing spawns countable. op_total for refusal_path_unanswerable is deliberately absent: that path short-circuits before any spawn, so its seam figure of 0 is already a whole-op 0. The counter's own hole is mechanism, not routing (it sees `subprocess.run`, not `Popen`/`os.posix_spawn`/`asyncio.create_subprocess_exec`); that precondition is enforced per-site by that gate's `test_legitimized_site_mechanism_pins_hold`. `op_total_pending_drain_superseded`=39, measured 2026-08-19: the pending_drain_superseded shape's own 23 `git_native._git` calls PLUS 16 more `subprocess.run` calls the seam cannot see -- the fixture's own scratch-clone/direct-URL setup calls are excluded (the counter is scoped to the `_handler` invocation only, `_count_op_spawns_both_ways`'s own docstring), so the +16 is entirely inside the invocation: `auto_push.drain_pending_push`'s read of the pending record, `_branch_resolves_locally`, `run_push_with_retry`'s own `rev-parse` reads (local_sha, old_remote_sha for the cockpit-touched check), `push_once`'s own rejected push (site 1), `_is_superseded`'s fetch plus `_is_ancestor`'s `merge-base --is-ancestor` (site 2), and `_invoke_cockpit_publish`'s own child process (site 3, the DoE publish script) -- this is exactly the three previously-`_UNCOUNTED_MEASURED_UNREACHED`-then-`_LEGITIMIZED_SITES` sites this fixture exists to discharge, none of it routed through `git_native._git` by construction (`auto_push` is a hook with callers outside this pipeline; rerouting it was rejected for the same reason the other three op_total deltas were). `deferred_diverged_detach`=20 seam / `op_total_deferred_diverged_detach`=26, opro-03 follow-up, measured 2026-08-21 (corrected same day -- an initial 28 recorded from a single early run did not reproduce across three subsequent independent runs, all reading 26; 26 is the figure carried here): the LAST reachable-and-uncounted site `test_no_uncounted_spawn_on_budgeted_path.py` flagged after C6 -- `auto_push._detach_and_run`'s Windows respawn `subprocess.Popen`, reached via `commit_scoped`'s private-index (diverged-path) branch's own `_replay_post_commit_auto_push` call (`git_native.py`, fires only when `suppress_post_commit_auto_push` is False, i.e. the default `push_mode='deferred'`, never on the `sync`/`never` shapes the other four fixtures use). This site spawns via `Popen`, not `run`, so the pre-existing `subprocess.run`-only op_total counter could never see it regardless of reachability; `_count_op_spawns_both_ways` was widened to also count `Popen`, scoped to the one recognized auto-push-respawn argv shape so it never intercepts `subprocess.run`'s own internal `Popen` calls (see that function's own docstring). `test_no_uncounted_spawn_on_budgeted_path.py`'s `_GLOBAL_SUBPROCESS_SPAWN` is the mechanism pin admitting this counter shape. This shape's own seam figure (20) already includes the two 2026-08-20 additions (`323aafaf8`/`82dc080eb`, see the sibling `_rationale` field) since it was measured after both landed -- it is a SEPARATE shape from the other four (a diverged path, not the agree branch), not a re-baseline of any of them.

ceremony.scoped_git_commit._c10_cold_end_to_end_rationale: C10 (this dispatch, state/dispatch-briefs/2026-08-22-a-commit-is-one-spawn-not-eleven/C10.md), measured 2026-08-23 against `git_native.commit_scoped()` directly (git_native.py:2959) -- NOT through the `ceremony.scoped_git_commit` OP HANDLER, which still calls the separate, unrewired `run_commit_pipeline` (`scoped_git_commit.py`'s own body, confirmed by grep -- `git_native.commit_scoped` is the C8a/C8b/C9 rebuild target but is not yet wired as this op's `_handler`). The 2026-08-23 baseline probe (`state/audits/2026-08-23-scoped-git-commit-cold-baseline-probe.py`, commit `47609183a`) already measured the OP-HANDLER path's own cold cost (1,174.5ms/41 processes by control) and explicitly deferred the POST-REBUILD number to this plan -- this entry is that number, for the rebuilt COMMITTER function, not the still-unrewired op. REGIME: bare interpreter with the lazy op-registration channel armed (`sys._coordinator_core_lazy_ops = True`, matching `invoke/__main__.py`/`cc_invoke.py`), confirming C7's 'fourth regime' hypothesis in `state/audits/2026-08-22-the-commit-path-cannot-reach-400ms-cold-because-of-the-ops-package.md` -- a fresh `import coordinator_core.ops.ceremony.git_native` under this regime measured 85.9-99.6ms process time (n=3, k=8), consistent with that audit's own 101.6ms LAZY figure for the same import, not the 475.3ms EAGER figure nor a sibling op's 15.6ms engine-cold/359.4ms bare-interpreter pair -- this op has no warm-engine-served production path today (it is SUSPENDED), so 'not warm' here means exactly this regime, not engine-cold. MEASURED (default `suppress_post_commit_auto_push=False`, i.e. the real `push_mode='deferred'` production default): isolated op cost 492.2-549.5ms process time, 10 spawns -- OVER the 400ms cold bar. ATTRIBUTED, not shrugged: a `git_native._git` seam spy on the same scenario shows only TWO native-git-seam spawns (one batched `--no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v2 -z --no-renames -- <25 paths>` divergence probe, one `interpret-trailers`) -- the residue is `hooks/auto_push.py`'s own post-commit replay check, which `git_native.py`'s own docstring says 'fires only when suppress_post_commit_auto_push is False', and which routes through `auto_push.py::_run_git`, OUTSIDE the `git_native._git` seam -- the exact uncounted bypass surface this manifest's `pending_drain_superseded`/`deferred_diverged_detach` entries already name, not a new one. CONFIRMED by toggling the flag: `suppress_post_commit_auto_push=True` drops isolated cost to 281.2ms / 6 spawns -- UNDER the 400ms bar. DISPOSITION: the committer's OWN cost (net of scaffolding: ~90-100ms lazy import + ~281ms of its own git/in-process work for 25 paths) is within budget; the auto-push replay check's ~210-270ms/4-spawn residue is a separate, already-documented bypass-surface cost this chunk's writes scope does not authorize fixing (and `op_budget_suspension.py` is explicitly out of scope for this chunk). Flagged for whichever chunk reinstates the op or wires `commit_scoped` into `scoped_git_commit`'s own `_handler` -- not fixed here.
ceremony.scoped_git_commit._2026_08_23_query_spawn_cut_rationale: Re-baselined DOWNWARD 2026-08-23 by DIRECT MEASUREMENT against this suite's own five fixtures, every figure read off the failing assertion. 20->15, 21->16, 23->19, 34->28, 18->14. Deltas are NOT uniform (-5,-5,-4,-6,-4): a shape reaches a different subset of these reads, and predicting a constant would have shipped wrong keys -- which is the failure the entry above records ('written from the PLANNED shape, not measured against the LANDED code', never shipped green). This entry was itself written twice for that reason: an intermediate re-baseline (16/17/20/31/15) was measured, then superseded by these figures when a second author's change landed in the same commit. Only the final measured set is recorded; the intermediate one never shipped. FOUR REMOVALS, THREE AUTHORS' WORTH OF CONTEXT, all in one commit because budget-manifest.json's exact-equality assertion means code and manifest cannot be split: (1) `scoped_git_commit._repo_has_remote` no longer spawns `git remote` -- that subcommand only enumerates `[remote "..."]` section headers, so the process bought a text transform of a file this process can open. Reads the COMMON dir's config (remotes are not worktree-private) and fails OPEN on an unreadable config OR on an `[include]`/`[includeIf]` directive it cannot follow correctly -- git honours includes and a section scan does not, and a wrong False here sends an operator chasing a remote that exists. (2) `git/git_state.head_blobs` memoised on HEAD's own sha: three identical `ls-tree` spawns per commit down to one. Correct by construction rather than by discipline -- the answer is a projection of HEAD's tree, so anything that could change it moves HEAD and misses the key. Copy-on-return, because `git_native` merges freshness re-reads into what it gets back. (3) `git_native.rev_parse_head` reads `git_state.head_sha()` instead of spawning `git rev-parse HEAD` -- same resolution (`.git/HEAD` plus loose ref or packed-refs), from files. Eight production call sites, several twice per commit. Deliberately NOT memoised, unlike (2): three of those sites exist to observe that HEAD MOVED, so a HEAD-keyed cache would be useless or wrong. (4) claude-klabauter-c1's, in their words: `commit_authored_content` called `git_state.head_blobs()` unconditionally before the fast-path fork, so the in-process arm still paid a `git ls-tree` spawn it did not need. It now reads HEAD's tree spine in process via C3's `read_tree_spine` and falls back to `head_blobs` only when the spine is unreadable -- which is the same condition that sends the commit to the ladder anyway. Both arms answer the same question of the same source, HEAD's tree, so the 'does not exist in HEAD' refusal is identical either way. New helper `_head_entry_for`. This is a process-count reduction, not a routing tidy-up: AC1 measured at the `git_native._git()` seam read 3 while the leg actually issued 4 processes, because `head_blobs` reaches git through `run_git` and never crosses that seam. WHY THE SEAM KEYS DO NOT MOVE, and it is the entry above's own point paying off twice in one day: (2) and (4) reach the process boundary through `git/run.py::run_git`, which calls `subprocess.run` directly and never crosses the `git_native._git` name the seam counter wraps. Seam keys are UNCHANGED and were not edited; no seam assertion failed in any of the five shapes. DO NOT DIFF A SEAM KEY AGAINST AN op_total KEY -- they answer different questions, and that confusion produced a withdrawn '-5' in the entry above. Author (4) found their own defect by reading that warning rather than by being bitten by it. THESE ARE REMOVALS, NOT A BYPASS BEING PAPERED OVER, which is the distinction this assertion's failure message asks for: no new uncounted path was introduced, four spawns stopped happening. THE OP REMAINS SUSPENDED. These figures are a baseline for its reinstatement case (state/handoffs/2026-08-21-earn-ceremony-scoped-git-commit-back-und.md), NOT a claim it meets the PM's 400ms cold bar. It does not: measured by control before these cuts, the handler cost 1,174.5ms process time and 41 processes. Four spawns is not that gap.

Fix: `_batch_resolve_commits` resolves the whole token set in ONE `git cat-file --batch-check` process (stdin-fed, `timeout=_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT`), each token queried as `{tok}^{commit}` to match the prior per-token `rev-parse --verify -q {tok}^{commit}` peel byte-for-byte -- the set of tokens classified as resolving to a commit is unchanged, only the spawn shape is. `target_ms`/`tolerance` satisfy `budget.py._validated_budget`'s required override shape only; `spawn_count_budget` is the enforced invariant, guarded by `coordinator_core/ops/test_changelog_cited_in_range_spawn_bound.py`. `n_tokens=1`: any nonzero number of distinct tokens costs exactly one subprocess (was N before the fix). `no_tokens=0`: an empty token set short-circuits before spawning at all.

bin.coordinator_harvest_deferrals_dedup_._rationale: 2026-08-15 audit (state/audits/2026-08-15-fleet-composed-op-spawn-census.md row 13 / state/audits/2026-08-15-fleet-census-reverification-at-head.md): `coordinator-harvest-deferrals.py::_harvest`'s per-row loop calls `_candidate_search_dirs(row)` for every candidate, which in turn calls `_repo_root()` (a `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` subprocess spawn), `_resolved_doe_root()`, and `_resolved_claude_klabauter_root()` (each capable of its own machine-local-registry/marketplace-cache subprocess spawn) FRESH per row -- 3 resolution calls x N rows for an answer invariant for the whole process's lifetime. The per-row WRITE dispatch itself (`_run_queue_append`/`_run_lesson_promote`, already timeout-bounded at `_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT_SECS`, and since the 2026-08-15 staff review also catches `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` and degrades it to a per-row failure) is deliberately left one-spawn-per-row -- each row's write stays isolated via the `_run_*` helpers' return-False contract, not a `try` inside `_harvest()` itself, so one row's failure or hang never blocks another's. Fix (root resolution): memoize the three resolution calls (`_repo_root_cache`/`_resolved_doe_root_cache`/`_resolved_claude_klabauter_root_cache`, first-call-wins, mirroring the pre-existing `_CLI_CMD_CACHE` pattern). Fix (directory scan, 2026-08-15 staff review Defect 2 -- the expensive half of the per-row work an earlier pass left unhoisted): `_already_harvested` re-globbed AND re-read EVERY `*.yaml` file in up to four directories (`state/improvement-queue`, `state/lessons-outbox`, in both claude-klabauter and DoE) ONCE PER CANDIDATE ROW -- `_derive_proposed_action`'s own docstring measures those corpora at 605/493 entries, i.e. O(rows x ~1100 full file reads) for a key set invariant across the loop. `_collect_evidence_lines(search_dirs)` now does that glob+read ONCE, before the loop, returning the flat list of `evidence:`-prefixed lines; `_already_harvested(key, evidence_lines)` is then an O(1)-per-row substring membership check against that pre-collected list, preserving the exact prior match semantics (line must start with `evidence:`, key checked via substring). `target_ms`/`tolerance` are carried only to satisfy `budget.py._validated_budget`'s required override shape -- this key is not a real op, `spawn_count_budget` is the enforced invariant. Enforced by `coordinator/bin/tests/test_harvest_deferrals_dedup_scan_memoized.py` (`resolution_calls_for_5_candidate_rows=2` -- exactly one SPAWN each from `_resolved_doe_root()`/`_resolved_claude_klabauter_root()` regardless of candidate-row count, fixture: 5 rows, versus 15 pre-fix; lowered from 3 to 2 on 2026-08-17 because eacbba04a routed `_repo_root()` through `coordinator_core.git.repo_root.show_toplevel`, which walks for the ordinary case and spawns only when the walk finds no `.git` entry -- the budget counts spawns, so that third call is no longer one. Memoization of all three is unchanged and still asserted; do NOT raise this back to 3 to make a regression pass) and `coordinator/bin/tests/test_harvest_deferrals_evidence_scan_hoisted.py` (`directory_scan_calls_for_5_candidate_rows=1` -- `_collect_evidence_lines`/the underlying `glob.glob`+file-read pass runs exactly once per `_harvest()` invocation regardless of candidate-row count, versus once per row pre-fix; asserts the CALL COUNT of the scan, not wall-clock).

bin.workday_complete_close_backfill_disp._rationale: 2026-08-15 audit (state/audits/2026-08-15-fleet-composed-op-spawn-census.md row 14): `workday-complete-close.py::cmd_backfill_dispatch_rows` dispatches ONE full composed step9-ceremony subprocess (`_dispatch_step9_row`) per gap date, up to the 14-day lookback -- deliberately left one-spawn-per-gap-date: each row's exit code is tracked independently and the loop's own contract ('one bad day should not abandon the rest of the backfill') requires row N's failure to never block row N+1's dispatch, so batching into a single invocation is NOT equivalent and was rejected. `_dispatch_step9_row`'s previously-unbounded `subprocess.run` now carries `timeout=_STEP9_ROW_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_SECS` (120s), with a `TimeoutExpired` caught and converted to a per-row failure (rc=1) rather than crashing the whole loop, preserving per-row isolation under a timeout the same as under a subprocess failure. `target_ms`/`tolerance` are carried only to satisfy `budget.py._validated_budget`'s required override shape -- this key is not a real op. 2026-08-15 staff review: a prior `spawn_count_budget.spawns_per_gap_date=1` was removed here -- it was N==N (true by definition for any one-spawn-per-row implementation, bounds nothing) and its docstring wording actively forbade the correct duplicate-date dedup fix (workday-complete-close.py::cmd_backfill_dispatch_rows now skips a re-seen date rather than re-dispatching it), which would have made a 3-row input with one duplicate cost 2 spawns and broken that tautological assertion. The real invariants (timeout present on every row dispatch; a duplicated date dispatches once, not twice; one row's timeout does not abort the rest) are behavioural, not spawn-count-shaped, and are enforced directly by `coordinator/bin/tests/test_workday_complete_backfill_dispatch_timeout.py` without a manifest budget.

ops.discover_working_repos._spawn_count_rationale: Two LAYERS of key, deliberately. The op_total_* keys are the OP: main() end-to-end, nothing stubbed, measured 2026-08-19 (opro-03 C6) at 3 / 3 / 0 for the Tier-A-non-empty, Tier-B-fallback and all-tiers-empty shapes. That shell-out is a SANCTIONED carve-out (test_no_bash_dependency.py names it, for byte-parity with the bash oracle), so it is counted, not removed; reducing it is a carve-out decision, not a budget one. The other two keys are SUB-PATHS and must not be read as the op total: per_call=1 is _tier_a5 alone, and machine_local_cli_elimination_calls=0 isolates _merged_flat_registry's elimination of the per-key machine-local CLI spawns, legitimately stubbing _sort_unique to do so. History worth keeping: per_call was 0 until 2026-08-19 because the asserting test monkeypatched out _sort_unique -- the one function on that path that spawns -- immediately before counting, so the figure was true of a stubbed op and false of this one. The op total went unmeasured for longer still because _tier_a reads Path.home()/.claude/projects and the pre-existing COORDINATOR_TIER_A_FS_ROOT seam covers only the existence probe; COORDINATOR_TIER_A_PROJECTS_DIR was added to make a hermetic main() count possible at all. No spawn was ever added by any of this -- each raise made an existing spawn countable. Trace: state/audits/2026-08-19-opro-03-c08-budgeted-op-spawn-trace.md.
ops.discover_working_repos._rationale: 2026-08-15 staff review of the fleet spawn sweep (state/audits/2026-08-15-fleet-census-reverification-at-head.md). discover_working_repos.py::_tier_a5 spawned one machine-local keys subprocess plus one machine-local get <key> per repos.* key, and ::_publish_mirror_keys independently repeated the whole pattern for publish.mirrors.*.path -- measured live at ~24 interpreter spawns per main() call (19 repos keys + 4 mirror paths), each with a 10s timeout, on a box CLAUDE.md sizes at 50-70 concurrent LLM sessions. This was not merely slow: it contradicted the standing negative spec in coordinator_core/machine_resolver.py, which forbids shelling out to that CLI, and the 2026-08-05 PM directive on de-bashing spawn amplification that it records. It was also LESS CORRECT than a direct read -- registry_get's docstring notes the CLI lives under a resettable bin directory, so the CLI working is not proof of reset-survival, while a direct file read is. Fix: _merged_flat_registry merges registry.local.toml over registry.toml via machine_resolver.load_flat_registry_file/registry_dir (direct tomllib), zero subprocesses. Concern-layer parity was verified rather than assumed: _machine_local.py::_flatten_nested documents these keys as root-namespace-only and actively drops concern-name collisions, so a flat two-file read cannot miss a repo. target_ms/tolerance satisfy budget.py._validated_budget's required override shape only; spawn_count_budget is the enforced invariant, guarded by coordinator_core/ops/test_discover_working_repos_spawn_budget.py. per_call=0 is a real ceiling, not a per-item ratio -- any key count costs zero subprocesses, so a regression to the CLI fails at 1.

Cite d728c37cb and 65bbe1323's commit messages for post-fix AC2/AC3 evidence, not this block.

_hook_seam_http_transport.unit_note: BOTH units recorded on purpose. Wall is what a blocking PreToolUse hook makes the operator wait; process time is what isolates work from queueing on a box running dozens of sessions. Neither alone is the cost.

http_warm.shape: in-process POST to a resident loopback listener (127.0.0.1 literal), adapter parses the reply
http_warm.wall_p50_instability_note: p50 moved 0.6 -> 14.4ms across three runs minutes apart with identical code; min held at 0.44-0.61 throughout. The spread is peer load, not this transport. Do not quote a p50 from a single run as this arm cost.

cold_interpreter_plus_engine_import.shape: python3 -c "import coordinator_core.ipc" -- the floor every hook fire pays today

cold_bare_interpreter.shape: python3 -c pass -- interpreter start alone, no engine

_hook_seam_http_transport.claim: The transport removes ONE PROCESS per hook fire. Re-measured 2026-08-25 that process costs ~27-32ms of child process time, not the ~47.7ms recorded on 2026-08-23. AC13 must not be claimed met off any wall run, and cannot be claimed at all while p(listener up) is zero.
_hook_seam_http_transport.not_yet_measured: End-to-end with a REAL guard op on the resident server. These arms measure the transport, not the guard work that rides it.

reverification.why: The 2026-08-23 rows entered the repo through a human safety sweep (8350b8fa0), never through their own session's commit, and no gate ran against them. Re-measured before anything was built on them.
reverification.method: coordinator_core.benchmarks.process_time.batched_process_time_ms, k=20, five independent repeats per arm, 2026-08-25 on the same box.
reverification.verdict: The 2026-08-23 figures (38.281 / 47.656) DO NOT REPRODUCE. Five repeats of each arm sit ~1.5x below them and outside their spread. The direction survives -- the transport removes one whole child process -- but the magnitude is ~27-32ms of child process time per hook fire, not ~47.7ms, and the engine-import increment over a bare interpreter is ~4-5ms, not ~9.4ms.
reverification.retracted_claim: "That figure is stable" is withdrawn. Both arms sit within two Windows scheduler ticks (~15.6ms) of each other, so a single k=20 batch cannot separate them; only the repeat spread can, and the spread is what moved.

c4_supervised_listener.method: Listener bound IN-PROCESS around the production supervisor._make_handler; arms interleaved round-robin, n=30, 3 warmup rounds discarded. Every primitive measured is the real one.
c4_supervised_listener.not_exercised: ensure_listener's spawn_detached leg. Spawning a resident process on a box running 50-70 sessions to take a number is the litter class the is_engine_root gate exists to prevent. Boot latency is therefore NOT in any figure below.
c4_supervised_listener.reads_the_p90_correctly: min and p50 sit under 0.7ms on all three arms; p90 jumps to ~14-15ms on the two that touch a socket. That is PEER LOAD, not transport cost -- the same 0.6 -> 14.4ms movement the 2026-08-23 rows recorded across runs with identical code, now reproduced within a single interleaved run. Quote min alongside any p50; never quote a p90 from this box as an arm cost.

p_listener_up.why: NOT SAMPLABLE IN THIS REPO, and that is correct behaviour rather than a gap. current_engine_clone() resolves to X:/claude-klabauter, which is unstamped by design; ensure_listener's is_engine_root gate therefore refuses to start a listener here, so p(listener up) is structurally zero on this clone no matter what C2 and C3 wired.
p_listener_up.surface_where_it_exists: X:/claude-klabauter, the stamped publish clone that carries production hook traffic. Sampling it is a cross-repo action with its own owner, not something this plan takes unilaterally.
p_listener_up.what_would_close_it: A run of the discovery+health arms above from inside a stamped clone, over n>=25 spread across a real session's lifetime, reporting p(listener up) with its n.
